chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Getting paid by Luckey Roberts: the union hearing and the wrong address
summary: Danny had to take Roberts to the union to be paid after six months, and Roberts gave wrong addresses because he kept three women.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: If you worked with Luckey Roberts, you never got your money til later. I played a gig with him, it was six months; I had to bring him to the union to get paid. When I get to the union, he's there, and he's been ...(?)... it all before (?) like that. And he's there, and you go before the board for a hearing. "Mr. Roberts, I just come here to get my money. I don't want to push you or demand anything or cause no trouble. I just want my check." So he gives me twenty dollars to go to the Tuxedo Club with (?), and (?) to get back the next morning some time. That's the first and last time I played with him. Everybody played with him there a week.

You see, when he gives you... When he'd tell you to come to his house, he'd give you the wrong address. You'd knock on his White neighbor's house over on 164th Street, and she said, "Listen, I'm tired of people coming here. No Mister Roberts stayed here." Because he was keeping three women at all times, in different apartments. A maniac.
He was a little short guy, wide as he was tall almost.
Yeah, he looked like a little crocodile.
